changes.rationale: November 3 joint release and primary merger filing establish Canyon Bridge definitive acquisition at $8.30 per share. SEC litigation record also documents announcement-day price gain. Correct legacy impossible post-election label: election had not occurred. Class 2 target M&A applies; no assertion that deal ultimately closed.

June 16 contemporaneous market report directly attributes Coty rally to reported winning bid for P&G beauty assets. Class 2 reviewed acquirer-news exception covers attributed transaction reports before definitive agreement. Later primary deal release confirms transaction structure, but is not first-public evidence; do not backdate July agreement as June definitive takeout.

Primary issuer release dated August 10 announces nTelos acquisition and August 11 8 a.m. call; later issuer filings describe announcement August 11. Class 2 acquirer/Sprint partnership candidates are supported, but earliest August 10 publication time and direct August 11 price attribution remain unresolved. Preserve date discrepancy.

Primary counterparty release establishes AirCard asset sale January 28 and January 29 morning call; trade account directly attributes SWIR gain to divestiture. This is business-asset sale, not takeover of all Sierra Wireless. Class 2/11 strategic-disposal eligibility needs resolution. Preliminary results in NETGEAR release belong to buyer, not automatically SWIR earnings.

Primary filings establish termination of Mitel proposed Polycom acquisition and $60 million break fee. Expanded class 2 acquirer exception does not automatically resolve eligibility of an abandoned acquisition; class 11 strategic repricing is plausible but not a new sale process for Mitel. Preserve termination rather than describe Mitel as takeover target or simple financing.
